overview: Wrap the native video element in a media adapter. Feed actual media events into a state machine instead of assuming play() succeeded. Use native HLS where supported or a compatible adaptive player via Media Source Extensions; quality selection follows capabilities and user preference. The graph separates browser interaction state, server query state and the existing backend. It is one defensible approach; equivalent boundaries and well-argued alternatives are welcome.
limitations: Design checks inspect structure and written evidence only; they do not execute a UI or prove accessibility/performance.

estimation.assumption: 5 Mb/s stream; illustrative 20 s buffered media
estimation.calculation: 5 × 20 / 8 = 12.5 MB encoded payload, excluding decoder overhead
estimation.result: Do not equate JavaScript heap with media memory or prefetch the whole movie
estimation.implication: Measure startup delay, rebuffer ratio, seek latency and decoder behavior on supported devices.

components.purpose: Keyboard, pointer, touch and assistive-technology entry point. Client architecture only; backend internals are external dependencies.
components.rationale: Own this responsibility at the Browser / User boundary; keep communication explicit through the diagrammed dependency.

components.purpose: Wrap the native video element in a media adapter. Feed actual media events into a state machine instead of assuming play() succeeded. Use native HLS where supported or a compatible adaptive player via Media Source Extensions; quality selection follows capabilities and user preference. Performance plan: One active player per page; lazy comments/recommendations, defer optional player modules; bound prefetch and release the previous source on navigation. Accessibility: Prefer usable native controls as fallback, labelled custom controls, keyboard seeking/volume and visible focus. Provide captions and avoid autoplay with sound; handle play() rejection. Failure recovery: Refresh authorization once, preserve intended time, resume only after metadata is valid; show retry and keep controls operable. A new video ID cancels old loads. Trade-off: Native playback minimizes complexity but gives less control over adaptive logic. A player library adds capabilities and bundle weight; DRM/browser matrices require explicit scope.

flows.title: Local interaction, state transition and UI update

steps.title: Receive user intent
steps.explanation: Load playback metadata and choose native or adaptive playback support. Prefer usable native controls as fallback, labelled custom controls, keyboard seeking/volume and visible focus. Provide captions and avoid autoplay with sound; handle play() rejection.

steps.title: Apply the owning transition
steps.explanation: Wrap the native video element in a media adapter. Feed actual media events into a state machine instead of assuming play() succeeded. Use native HLS where supported or a compatible adaptive player via Media Source Extensions; quality selection follows capabilities and user preference.

steps.title: Render controlled child state
steps.explanation: One active player per page; lazy comments/recommendations, defer optional player modules; bound prefetch and release the previous source on navigation. Child events return to the owner; focus and selection use stable identities.

steps.title: Call or subscribe to the feature dependency
steps.explanation: Keep imperative media lifecycle isolated from declarative page and controls. Refresh authorization once, preserve intended time, resume only after metadata is valid; show retry and keep controls operable. A new video ID cancels old loads.

steps.title: Capture user intent without duplicating authority
steps.explanation: Validate local input and enter a pending state. Use the component callback rather than mutating server snapshots directly.

steps.title: Send the versioned operation
steps.explanation: Call PUT /videos/{id}/progress through the API adapter. Request: {positionSeconds:245,sessionId:"play1",updatedAt:"..."}. A prior successful response or unresolved operation must not be overwritten by a stale retry.

steps.title: Reconcile or expose recovery
steps.explanation: Refresh authorization once, preserve intended time, resume only after metadata is valid; show retry and keep controls operable. A new video ID cancels old loads. Update the query key with the acknowledged version or invalidate/refetch it; maintain focus and make pending/error state visible.

steps.title: Resolve playback authorization
steps.explanation: Load metadata from backend; validate entitlement and expiration before assigning the source to the media adapter.

steps.title: Fetch the media stream
steps.explanation: The adapter/native video pipeline requests the manifest and bounded segments directly from Media CDN. Buffering, seeking and source cleanup are driven by actual media events.

failureCases.scenario: Signed manifest expires during a seek or network drops
failureCases.handling: Refresh authorization once, preserve intended time, resume only after metadata is valid; show retry and keep controls operable. A new video ID cancels old loads.

failureCases.scenario: Route or identity changes while work is in flight
failureCases.handling: Dispose subscriptions, abort obsolete reads and ignore old generations; partition/clear private cache before showing a new account. Preserve only explicitly safe drafts.
